answer.text: Buying a put option on an asset you already own (long stock + long put) — maximum loss = stock purchase price - put strike + premium, while retaining unlimited upside potential
Selling a put option to generate income on a stock you own
Buying a call option to protect against stock price declines
Shorting the underlying stock and buying a put as insurance

explanation.text: The Logic: Protective put = Long stock + Long put. If the stock falls below the put strike K, the put compensates for the loss below K. Maximum loss = stock purchase price - put strike + premium. When the put strike equals the stock purchase price, the maximum loss is just the premium. The upside remains unlimited (net of the premium paid). The Trap: Selling a put generates income (cash-secured put) but does not protect a long stock position. A call protects against missing upside, not downside. Shorting stock plus a put is a different strategy. Note: The downside-risk formula uses stock purchase price minus strike, not strike minus stock price.
